title: Bread and Butter Pudding
subtitle: Buttered bread baked in a vanilla custard
excerpt: Slices of buttered white bread layered with raisins and soaked in a rich vanilla custard, then baked until the top is golden and crisp and the inside is soft and yielding. The best of British puddings.

recipe.sourceNotes: Bread and butter pudding has been a British household staple since the 13th century, when early versions used stale bread and sweet spiced liquids. The modern form with sliced buttered bread, custard, and raisins was established by the 18th century. It is a dish designed around using up stale bread. Brioche or croissant make a richer version, but standard white bread gives a more traditional result with a better contrast between the crisp top and the soft, custard-soaked interior.

recipeTools.notes: A medium oven-proof dish, roughly 25 x 18 cm.

content.text: Leave the pudding to soak for at least 30 minutes before baking: this allows the custard to fully saturate the bread. Bake in a bain-marie (the dish set in a roasting tin of hot water) if you want a very soft interior; bake directly if you prefer more crisp top. The pudding is done when the custard is just set but still trembles slightly in the centre.
Butter the bread generously on one side. Cut each slice into triangles. Arrange overlapping in a buttered oven-proof dish, butter-side up. Scatter the raisins between the layers.
Whisk together the milk, cream, eggs, caster sugar, vanilla, and nutmeg. Pour slowly over the bread. Press the bread gently to submerge. Leave to soak for at least 30 minutes.

Heat the oven to 170 C / fan 150 C / gas 3. Sprinkle the demerara sugar over the top. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the custard is just set and the top is golden. Leave to rest for 5 minutes. Serve warm with cream or custard.
